title: "TVAR"

In the course on Bayesian time series modeling we talked about TVAR an NDLM that covers time varying regression models, but we never did more than consider it as a theoretical construct and note that it is called a TVAR model. 

I did some work on estimating elasticities of demand but I never got around to modeling demand to a shopping cart with possibilities of substitutes and complements. Today I want to simulate demand time series based on such an elasticity matrix and see if I can recover the elasticity matrix from the data. 

I also did some work on RL and I think that for related products a model should be able to use a smaller information set to recover the matrix than for unrelated products. This ability to of a model to recover the matrix from fewer interventions and in less time presents a great cost saving for an automated a/b pricing system. If one this is correct it should allow the store manager to request a pricing schedule that recovers this matrix with minimal effort and in a brief time span. 

Note: that evaluating elasticities has an indexing problem and may require extended trials to uncover the demand function and requisite optima but in this case I want to look at just a small block of products.


## Step one pick Elasticizes and generate a demand data set


I want to try a TVAR model on the data. I will use the NDLM framework to do so. The NDLM framework is a generalization of the Kalman filter that allows us to handle non-linear systems and non-Gaussian noise. It is a powerful tool for time series analysis and forecasting.


```{python}


from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from dataclasses import dataclass
from functools import partial
from typing import Callable
RNG = np.random.default_rng

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SimConfig:
    T: int = 240; n: int = 4
    market_relation: str = "complements"   # {"complements","substitutes","independent"}
    income_effect: bool = False
    own_elast: float = -1.1
    cross_mag: float = 0.25                # |cross elasticity|
    income_elast: float = 0.6              # normal goods
    ar_price: float = 0.85; ar_demand: float = 0.4; ar_income: float = 0.9
    price_vol: float = 0.04; demand_vol: float = 0.10; income_vol: float = 0.02
    season_amp: float = 0.15
    base_price: float = 10.0; base_demand: float = 100.0; base_income: float = 100.0
    shock_prob: float = 0.05; shock_scale: float = 0.15
    price_update_k: int = 1
    seed: int | None = 123

def _cross_sign(flag: str) -> float:
    return -1.0 if flag=="complements" else (1.0 if flag=="substitutes" else 0.0)

def elasticity_matrix(n: int, own: float, cross_mag: float, relation: str, rng) -> np.ndarray:
    cross = _cross_sign(relation)*cross_mag
    E = np.full((n,n), cross, float); np.fill_diagonal(E, own)
    E += 0.05*(rng.random((n,n))-0.5)  # small heterogeneity
    for i in range(n): E[i,i] = min(E[i,i], own)
    if relation=="complements":
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(n):
                if i!=j: E[i,j] = min(E[i,j], -1e-4)
    elif relation=="substitutes":
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(n):
                if i!=j: E[i,j] = max(E[i,j], +1e-4)
    else:
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(n):
                if i!=j: E[i,j] = 0.0
    return E

def price_process(n,T,ar,vol,base_price,shock_prob,shock_scale,k,rng):
    lp = np.log(base_price)*np.ones(n); out = np.zeros((T,n))
    for t in range(T):
        if t==0 or (k>0 and t%k==0):
            eps = vol*rng.standard_normal(n)
            jumps = (rng.random(n)<shock_prob)*(shock_scale*rng.standard_normal(n))
            lp = ar*lp + (1-ar)*np.log(base_price) + eps + jumps
        out[t]=lp
    return out

def income_process(T,ar,vol,base_income,rng):
    li = np.log(base_income); out=np.zeros(T)
    for t in range(T):
        li = ar*li + (1-ar)*np.log(base_income) + vol*rng.standard_normal()
        out[t]=li
    return out

def seasonality(t, amp): 
    w = 2*np.pi/12.0
    return amp*(0.6*np.sin(w*t)+0.4*np.cos(w*t))

def demand_fn_factory(cfg: SimConfig) -> Callable:
    rng = RNG(cfg.seed+11 if cfg.seed is not None else None)
    E = elasticity_matrix(cfg.n, cfg.own_elast, cfg.cross_mag, cfg.market_relation, rng)
    alpha = np.log(cfg.base_demand)*np.ones(cfg.n)
    def f(logP_t, s_t, u_t, prev_u, logY_t=None):
        innov = cfg.ar_demand*prev_u + (1-cfg.ar_demand)*u_t
        logQ = alpha + s_t + E@logP_t + innov
        if cfg.income_effect and logY_t is not None:
            logQ += cfg.income_elast*(logY_t - np.log(cfg.base_income))
        return logQ
    f.E = E; f.alpha = alpha
    return f

def simulate_products(T=240, n=4, market_relation="complements",
                      income_effect=False, price_update_k=1, seed=7):
    """
    Simulate n-product system. Returns (df_long, E). Writes CSVs:
    - products_demand_long.csv / products_demand_wide.csv / elasticities_flagged.csv
    - price: 2 dp; demand_thousands: 3 dp (Q/1000)
    """
    cfg = SimConfig(T=T,n=n,market_relation=market_relation,
                    income_effect=income_effect,price_update_k=price_update_k,seed=seed)
    rng = RNG(seed)
    logP = price_process(n,T,cfg.ar_price,cfg.price_vol,cfg.base_price,
                         cfg.shock_prob,cfg.shock_scale,cfg.price_update_k,rng)
    logY = income_process(T,cfg.ar_income,cfg.income_vol,cfg.base_income,rng) if cfg.income_effect else None
    f = demand_fn_factory(cfg); E=f.E
    u_prev=np.zeros(n); rows=[]
    for t in range(T):
        s_t = seasonality(np.array([t]), cfg.season_amp)[0]
        u_t = cfg.demand_vol*rng.standard_normal(n)
        logQ = f(logP[t], s_t, u_t, u_prev, (logY[t] if logY is not None else None))
        base = f.alpha + s_t + (E@logP[t]) + (cfg.income_elast*(logY[t]-np.log(cfg.base_income)) if logY is not None else 0.0)
        u_prev = logQ - base
        P = np.exp(logP[t]); Q = np.exp(logQ)
        for i in range(n):
            rows.append((t+1,f"prod_{i+1}", round(P[i],2), round(Q[i]/1000.0,3)))
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["t","product","price","demand_thousands"])
    if logY is not None:
        inc = pd.DataFrame({"t":np.arange(1,T+1),"income":np.round(np.exp(logY),2)})
        df = df.merge(inc, on="t", how="left")
    df.to_csv("data/100/demand/products_demand_long.csv",index=False)
    wide_Q = df.pivot(index="t",columns="product",values="demand_thousands").add_prefix("Qk_")
    wide_P = df.pivot(index="t",columns="product",values="price").add_prefix("P_")
    out = pd.concat([wide_P,wide_Q],axis=1).reset_index()
    if "income" in df.columns:
        out = out.merge(df[["t","income"]].drop_duplicates(), on="t", how="left")
    out.to_csv("data/100/demand/products_demand_wide.csv",index=False)
    em = pd.DataFrame(E, index=[f"Q_i(prod_{i+1})" for i in range(n)],
                         columns=[f"logP(prod_{j+1})" for j in range(n)])
    em.to_csv("data/100/demand/elasticities_flagged.csv")
    return df, E

# Demo (validates)
df_demo, E_demo = simulate_products(T=72, n=3,
                                    market_relation="complements",
                                    income_effect=True,
                                    price_update_k=1,
                                    seed=10)

```

## NDLM — NDLM elasticities MVP $\mathcal{R} code$

```{r}
#| label: ndlm-elasticities
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dlm); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(purrr)
  library(stringr); library(tibble); library(readr)
})

# --- Panel prep: Y = log(demand_thousands), X = [logP_all (+ log_income)] ---
make_panel <- function(df, period = 12) {
  stopifnot(all(c("t","product","price","demand_thousands") %in% names(df)))
  products <- sort(unique(df$product))

  P_wide <- df %>%
    select(t, product, price) %>%
    mutate(col = paste0("logP_", product)) %>%
    select(-product) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = col, values_from = price) %>%
    arrange(t) %>%
    mutate(across(starts_with("logP_"), log))

  has_income <- "income" %in% names(df)
  if (has_income) {
    INC <- df %>% distinct(t, income) %>% arrange(t) %>% mutate(log_income = log(income))
    P_wide <- left_join(P_wide, INC %>% select(t, log_income), by = "t")
  }

  panel <- map(products, function(pname) {
    di <- df %>% filter(product == pname) %>% arrange(t)
    dat <- di %>% select(t, y = demand_thousands) %>% left_join(P_wide, by = "t") %>% arrange(t)
    y <- log(pmax(dat$y, 1e-6))                     # guard log(0)
    xcols <- grep("^logP_", names(dat), value = TRUE)
    if (has_income) xcols <- c(xcols, "log_income")
    X <- as.matrix(dat[, xcols, drop = FALSE])
    list(product = pname, y = y, X = X, xnames = xcols, T = nrow(dat))
  })
  list(products = products, panel = panel, period = period, has_income = has_income)
}

# --- Fit one product: seasonality + static regression (betas as constant states, W=0) ---
fit_one_product <- function(y, X, period = 12, maxit = 200) {
  k <- ncol(X)
  nSeas <- period - 1

  buildFun <- function(par) {
    # V estimated; seasonal states fixed; regression betas (incl. intercept) fixed
    mod_seas <- dlmModSeas(period, dV = exp(par[1]), dW = rep(0, nSeas))
    mod_reg  <- dlmModReg(X, addInt = TRUE, dV = 0, dW = rep(0, k + 1))
    mod_seas + mod_reg
  }

  init <- log(var(y, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.2 + 1e-6)
  fit  <- dlmMLE(y, parm = init, build = buildFun, control = list(maxit = maxit))
  if (fit$convergence != 0) warning("dlmMLE did not report convergence (code=", fit$convergence, "). Proceeding.")

  mod  <- buildFun(fit$par)
  filt <- dlmFilter(y, mod)
  sm   <- dlmSmooth(filt)

  t_last <- length(y)
  # --- FIX: correct beta indices (start at nSeas + 1) ---
  idx_beta <- nSeas + seq_len(k + 1)
  # sanity
  m <- ncol(sm$s)
  stopifnot(length(idx_beta) == (k + 1), max(idx_beta) <= m)

  # Posterior mean and SEs at T
  beta_hat <- drop(sm$s[t_last, idx_beta])
  S_T <- dlmSvd2var(sm$U.S[[t_last]], sm$D.S[t_last, ])
  se_beta <- sqrt(diag(S_T))[idx_beta]

  list(Vhat = exp(fit$par[1]),
       beta_hat = beta_hat, se_beta = se_beta,
       idx_beta = idx_beta, mod = mod, filt = filt, sm = sm)
}

# --- Collect elasticities across products ---
assemble_results <- function(mp, fits) {
  products <- mp$products
  xnames_list <- map(mp$panel, "xnames")

  all_price_cols <- sort(unique(unlist(lapply(xnames_list, function(v) v[str_detect(v,"^logP_")]))))
  n <- length(products)
  E_hat <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n, ncol = length(all_price_cols),
                  dimnames = list(paste0("Q_i(", products, ")"), all_price_cols))

  est_long <- bind_rows(map2(mp$panel, fits, function(pu, fit) {
    tibble(product = pu$product,
           term    = c("(Intercept)", pu$xnames),
           estimate = fit$beta_hat,
           se       = fit$se_beta) |>
      mutate(lwr = estimate - 1.96 * se, upr = estimate + 1.96 * se)
  }))

  for (i in seq_along(products)) {
    this_x <- xnames_list[[i]]
    bh <- setNames(fits[[i]]$beta_hat[-1], this_x)   # drop intercept; name the rest
    for (col in this_x[str_detect(this_x, "^logP_")]) E_hat[i, col] <- bh[col]
  }
  list(E_hat = E_hat, est_long = est_long)
}

compare_with_truth <- function(E_hat, path_dir = "data/100/demand") {
  truth_file <- if (file.exists(file.path(path_dir, "elasticities.csv"))) {
    file.path(path_dir, "elasticities.csv")
  } else if (file.exists(file.path(path_dir, "elasticities_flagged.csv"))) {
    file.path(path_dir, "elasticities_flagged.csv")
  } else return(NULL)

  E_true <- read.csv(truth_file, check.names = FALSE)
  rownames(E_true) <- E_true[[1]]; E_true[[1]] <- NULL
  E_true <- as.matrix(E_true)

  common_rows <- intersect(rownames(E_hat), rownames(E_true))
  common_cols <- intersect(colnames(E_hat), colnames(E_true))
  Eh <- E_hat[common_rows, common_cols, drop = FALSE]
  Et <- E_true[common_rows, common_cols, drop = FALSE]

  tibble(
    q_row = rep(common_rows, each = length(common_cols)),
    p_col = rep(common_cols, times = length(common_rows)),
    est   = as.vector(Eh),
    true  = as.vector(Et),
    abs_err = abs(est - true),
    rel_err = abs(est - true) / pmax(1e-8, abs(true))
  )
}

# --- Main runner: reads your CSV, fits, writes outputs, and compares to truth if present ---
run_fit <- function(input_file = "data/100/demand/products_demand_long.csv",
                    out_dir    = "data/100/demand",
                    period = 12, maxit = 200) {
  df_long <- read.csv(input_file, check.names = FALSE)

  mp   <- make_panel(df_long, period = period)
  fits <- map(mp$panel, ~ fit_one_product(y = .x$y, X = .x$X, period = period, maxit = maxit))
  assembled <- assemble_results(mp, fits)

  dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  write.csv(round(assembled$E_hat, 6),
            file.path(out_dir, "fit_ndlm_elasticities.csv"),
            row.names = TRUE, na = "")
  write.csv(assembled$est_long,
            file.path(out_dir, "elasticity_estimates_long.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)

  cmp <- compare_with_truth(assembled$E_hat, out_dir)
  if (!is.null(cmp)) write.csv(cmp, file.path(out_dir, "elasticity_errors.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

  invisible(list(E_hat = assembled$E_hat, est = assembled$est_long, cmp = cmp, fits = fits))
}

# --- Example usage in your qmd ---
df_long <- read.csv("data/100/demand/products_demand_long.csv")
res <- run_fit()
e_raw <- read.csv("data/100/demand/fit_ndlm_elasticities.csv", check.names = FALSE)
head(e_raw)
if (file.exists("data/100/demand/elasticity_errors.csv")) read.csv("data/100/demand/elasticity_errors.csv") %>%
  summarise(RMSE = sqrt(mean((est - true)^2, na.rm = TRUE)),
            MedAbsErr = median(abs_err, na.rm = TRUE))

# # Example:
# res <- run_fit(
#   input_file = "data/100/demand/products_demand_long.csv",
#   out_dir    = "data/100/demand",
#   period = 12
)
```
